rows.question: My Limited Edition Beta copy of Lightning Bolt reads "Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: The card currently deals 3 damage to any target — its current Oracle wording, not the Beta printed wording, states what it does now.
Missing: None
Why: Your Beta copy carries the original printed text, which allowed only a single target. The current card document for Lightning Bolt gives the wording used for play today, and it says the damage can go to any target rather than one target. The difference matters because "any target" covers targets the 1993 wording did not name at all.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text, shown in the retrieved card document for Lightning Bolt. I retrieved no Comprehensive Rules paragraph stating that Oracle wording supersedes printed wording, so I cite no rule number for that point.
Quote [printed, Limited Edition Beta]: Lightning Bolt does 3 damage to one target.
Quote [current Oracle text]: Lightning Bolt deals 3 damage to any target.
Quote [current Oracle text, type line]: Instant
Rules: None
Conflict: The Beta printing says "one target"; the current Oracle text says "any target". The current Oracle wording controls what the card does now. No retrieved rule text was available to cite for that precedence, so the basis here is the current card document itself.
Sources: printing.b5d3dcab-2260-479d-9ef6-dfb92d4f6061, card.4457ed35-7c10-48c8-9776-456485fdf070

rows.question: My Limited Edition Alpha copy of False Orders reads "You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: The card no longer works as printed; under its current Oracle text it is an Instant that can only be cast during the declare blockers step, removes one target creature the defending player controls from combat, restores any blocks that depended solely on that creature, and then lets you have that creature block an attacking creature of your choice.
Missing: None
Why: The Alpha printing is a block-choice override: you decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, and it is played after blockers are chosen but before damage. The current Oracle wording instead removes the creature from combat and then optionally reassigns it to block an attacker of your choosing, with an explicit timing restriction to the declare blockers step. The two texts describe functionally different effects, so the Oracle text is what governs how the card behaves now.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text for False Orders, which supersedes the Limited Edition Alpha printing for how the card functions.
Quote (False Orders, Limited Edition Alpha, printed text): You decide whether and how one defending creature blocks, though you can't make a choice the defender couldn't legally make. Play after defender has chosen defense but before damage is dealt.
Quote (False Orders, current Oracle text): Instant
Cast this spell only during the declare blockers step.
Remove target creature defending player controls from combat. Creatures it was blocking that had become blocked by only that creature this combat become unblocked. You may have it block an attacking creature of your choice.
Rules: None
Conflict: The Alpha printed text (choose whether and how a defending creature blocks, played after blockers are declared) conflicts with the Oracle text (remove the creature from combat and optionally have it block a different attacker, castable only in the declare blockers step). The current Oracle wording wins.
Sources: printing.7eb71ac4-796d-4011-9002-1129bc09c284, card.38c5c952-8153-4d98-89b5-a75260383345

rows.question: My Unlimited Edition copy of Word of Command reads "You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Your Unlimited Edition copy uses the old wording, but the card is now defined by the Oracle text: you look at target opponent's hand, choose a card, control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving, and that player plays the card if able, with their mana abilities limited to lands they control.
Missing: None
Why: The printed Unlimited text and the current Oracle text describe the same spell but differ in detail: the printed version only says the opponent must play the chosen card immediately and cannot be countered once you have looked, while the Oracle wording spells out that you control the player during resolution and restricts which mana abilities that player may activate. The current rulings also confirm the timing — the opponent can respond to the spell before it resolves, and can still try to counter the spell you force them to cast. Where printed wording and Oracle wording disagree, the Oracle wording is what the card does.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text for Word of Command, which is the authoritative wording and supersedes the wording printed on older printings.

Quote [printed text, Unlimited Edition]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.

Quote [printed text, Limited Edition Alpha]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.

Quote [printed text, Limited Edition Beta]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.

Quote [current Oracle text]: Word of Command
Instant
Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving.

Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: Since this spell is an instant, your opponent gets a chance to respond to it as normal. Once this spell resolves, you look at your opponent's hand and choose a card. Note that it is common practice to respond to Word of Command by using up any spells or mana you have prior to letting it resolve.

Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: Your opponent can't counter the Word of Command after letting you look at their hand, but they can attempt to counter the spell you force them to cast.

Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: You must order your opponent to play the chosen card if it is possible to do so.

Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: You may Command your opponent to play a land (if they have not already done so this turn).

Rules: None relevant (CR 702.144a and CR 604.6 were retrieved but concern Demonstrate and static abilities that function from other zones; neither decides this question).

Conflict: The printed Unlimited wording omits the "you control that player" instruction and the restriction that the player may use mana abilities only from lands they control; the Oracle wording adds both, and the Oracle wording wins. The printed "may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand" survives in substance via the ruling that the opponent cannot counter Word of Command after letting you look, though they may still counter the spell you force them to cast.

Sources: printing.239c8547-207b-41d1-a2be-8825bfc6ef7f, printing.7d37b529-8a41-4177-abef-614f363e69d1, printing.96c21429-98d3-416b-be00-6aa9c4c5a006, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443#ruling5, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443#ruling6, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443#ruling8, card.e8ad3a77-b293-4d69-b080-27ca9f95d443#ruling9, comprehensive-rules-2026-09-25.txt#702.144a, comprehensive-rules-2026-09-25.txt#604.6

rows.question: My Fourth Edition copy of Mana Vault reads "Mana Vault does not untap during your untap phase. If it remains tapped during your upkeep, Mana Vault deals 1 damage to you. {4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep. ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: Your Fourth Edition Mana Vault now does exactly what its current Oracle text says: it doesn't untap in your untap step, you may pay {4} at the beginning of your upkeep to untap it, it deals 1 damage to you at the beginning of your draw step if it's still tapped, and it taps for {C}{C}{C}.

Missing: None

Why: The printed Fourth Edition wording is superseded by the current Oracle wording, which is the authoritative text for what a card does regardless of which printing you physically own. Two things changed materially: the damage moved from your upkeep to your draw step, and the untap payment changed from an activated ability usable only during your upkeep into a triggered ability at the beginning of your upkeep ("you may pay {4}"). The obsolete "interrupt" instruction on the old printing just means the mana ability works as a mana ability under current rules; "untap phase" is now the untap step.

Governing authority: Current Oracle text (card.736892cb-a34b-4bb9-b56c-e26e3db207a2), which governs the card's function over any printed wording.

Quote [Fourth Edition printed text, as supplied and confirmed by printing.3be9942c-89b3-422f-bb9d-b55f51a22a37]: Mana Vault does not untap during your untap phase. If it remains tapped during your upkeep, Mana Vault deals 1 damage to you.
{4}: Untap Mana Vault. Use this ability only during your upkeep.
ocT: Add three colorless mana to your mana pool. Play these additions as interrupts.

Quote [Current Oracle text (card.736892cb-a34b-4bb9-b56c-e26e3db207a2)]: This artifact doesn't untap during your untap step.
At the beginning of your upkeep, you may pay {4}. If you do, untap this artifact.
At the beginning of your draw step, if this artifact is tapped, it deals 1 damage to you.
{T}: Add {C}{C}{C}.

Rules: None

Conflict: The Fourth Edition wording deals the 1 damage during your upkeep and makes untapping an activated ability usable only during your upkeep; the current Oracle wording deals the damage at the beginning of your draw step and makes untapping an optional triggered ability at the beginning of your upkeep. The Oracle wording wins.

Sources: card.736892cb-a34b-4bb9-b56c-e26e3db207a2, printing.3be9942c-89b3-422f-bb9d-b55f51a22a37

rows.question: My Tempest copy of Mogg Fanatic reads "Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.". What does the card actually do now?
rows.answer:
Question type: printedVsOracle
Verdict: The card now does exactly what your Tempest copy says it does — the only difference is updated templating: the Oracle text is "Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target."
Missing: None
Why: The ability's function (sacrifice the Fanatic, deal 1 damage) is unchanged between the Tempest printing and the current Oracle wording; what changed is the template, using the self-referential "this creature" and the catch-all phrase "any target" in place of the card's own name and "target creature or player". One retrieved ruling is worth knowing in play: it is now too late to activate the ability once the Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage. Note that the retrieved evidence does not explain whether "any target" reaches anything the older phrase did not; it only supplies the two wordings.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text in the card document, which is the authoritative current wording; the Tempest printing document is used only as the comparison point. No Comprehensive Rules paragraph was retrieved for this answer.
Quote [printed — Tempest]: Sacrifice Mogg Fanatic: Mogg Fanatic deals 1 damage to target creature or player.
Quote [Oracle — current]: Sacrifice this creature: It deals 1 damage to any target.
Quote [ruling 2016-06-08]: Once Mogg Fanatic has dealt and been dealt combat damage, it's too late to activate its ability before it's destroyed.
Rules: None
Conflict: The Tempest printing's "Mogg Fanatic" and "target creature or player" disagree with Oracle's "this creature" and "any target"; the Oracle wording wins, and the disagreement is templating rather than a change in the sacrifice-for-1-damage effect. No retrieved source describes any functional difference between the two phrasings.
Sources: printing.ca2ecfd4-c874-4468-8601-87aa110d5a00, card.7efd5d62-6da2-428a-98e3-5b842f668656, card.7efd5d62-6da2-428a-98e3-5b842f668656#ruling0

rows.question: Can I register Windfall today, and in which formats? If it is restricted anywhere, say where.
rows.answer:
Question type: legality
Verdict: As of the 2026-09-18 snapshot in the retrieved evidence, Windfall can be registered in Vintage (restricted — one copy only), Commander, Duel and Oathbreaker, and cannot be registered in Legacy or Premodern, where it is banned; the evidence does not cover any other format.
Missing: Legality data for any format other than vintage, commander, duel, legacy, oathbreaker and premodern (e.g. Standard, Modern, Pioneer, Pauper, Historic) — none was retrieved. The snapshot date retrieved is 2026-09-18; no source confirms whether Windfall's status changed after that date, even though the corpus contains a Comprehensive Rules file dated 2026-09-25. The underlying banned/restricted announcement for Windfall itself was not retrieved (the only announcement link in evidence concerns a different card), so the status rests on the derived legality records.
Why: The retrieved legality records give Windfall's status per format on one stated date, and they agree on that date with no internal contradiction. Vintage is a restricted listing, so exactly one copy may be registered there, whereas the bannings in Legacy and Premodern mean zero copies. Formats not named in those records remain unaddressed, so the answer is confined to them. The retrieved CR 804.1 concerns the Emperor variant and has no bearing on card legality.
Governing authority: The dated format legality records for Windfall, with the current Oracle text in card.08becc07-28bc-4a2f-a6b0-28a2998d2f50 establishing the card's identity and current wording, under CR 108.1.

rows.question: When Word of Command resolves, who controls the opponent, and for how long?
rows.answer:
Question type: currentWording
Verdict: When Word of Command resolves, you (the caster) control the target opponent until Word of Command finishes resolving, and you continue to control that player while the chosen card resolves if it is cast as a spell.
Missing: None — though no Comprehensive Rules paragraph about controlling another player was retrieved; the answer rests on the Oracle text and the official rulings.
Why: The current Oracle text grants control of the target opponent for a bounded window tied to Word of Command's own resolution, and it separately extends that control through the resolution of the forced spell. The rulings confirm the practical consequences of that window without extending or shortening it.
Governing authority: Current Oracle text of Word of Command (the wording that governs how the card works), read together with its official rulings.
Quote [Oracle text — Word of Command, Instant]: Look at target opponent's hand and choose a card from it. You control that player until Word of Command finishes resolving. The player plays that card if able. While doing so, the player can activate mana abilities only if they're from lands that player controls and only if mana they produce is spent to activate other mana abilities of lands the player controls and/or to play that card. If the chosen card is cast as a spell, you control the player while that spell is resolving.
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: Since this spell is an instant, your opponent gets a chance to respond to it as normal. Once this spell resolves, you look at your opponent's hand and choose a card. Note that it is common practice to respond to Word of Command by using up any spells or mana you have prior to letting it resolve.
Quote [ruling 2011-01-01]: You must order your opponent to play the chosen card if it is possible to do so.
Quote [ruling 2016-07-13]: While controlling another player, you can see all cards in the game that player can see. This includes cards in that player's hand, face-down cards that player controls, and any cards in that player's library the player may look at.
Quote [printed text — Unlimited Edition, for contrast only]: You may look at opponent's hand and choose any card opponent can legally play using mana from his or her mana pool or lands. Opponent must play this card immediately; you make all the decisions it calls for. This spell may not be countered after you have looked at opponent's hand.
